title: Input rewind phase
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $start$ be a state of $M$, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $ok$ be a Boolean value. For any configuration $c$ of the three-state rewind machine on input $w$ whose state is $0$, there is a time $t$ no greater than the current input-head position plus $2$ such that the split-search round body, started from $c$ with its state relabeled as the rewind phase carrying $ok$, reaches a configuration whose state is $2$ and whose input-head position is $1$, with every other component unchanged, and with its state relabeled in the same way. At every time from $0$ through $t$, the run avoids the anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration with $M.k+1$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, three control states, and input $w$
replaced:
For a configuration $c$ of the rewind machine in its start state, there is a
time $t \le i + 2$, with $i$ the current input position, such that the round
body run from the rewind-phase embedding of $c$ (carrying the acceptance bit)

in the rewind machine's return state; the whole trace avoids the anchor and
